q-93738.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $P$ above. Find the matrix of the quadratic form ${x}^{T}\,Ax$ in the basis that consists of the columns of $P.$
q-93738.worked_solution:
Recall that if $x=[{x}_{1},{x}_{2}]^{T}$ is a vector given by its coordinates in the standard basis and $y=[{y}_{1},{y}_{2}]^{T}$ is the same vector but given in the coordinates relative to the basis that consists of the columns of $P,$ then 

$$
x=Py.
$$

As a result, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =(Py)^{T}\,A\,(Py) \\  & =({y}^{T}{P}^{T})\,A\,(Py) \\  & ={y}^{T}({P}^{T}\,AP)\,y,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that the matrix of our form in the new basis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{T}\,AP & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 6 \\ 4 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 13 \\ 13 & 14\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-94171.name: Question 2
q-94171.problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}$ in terms of the components of $y.$
q-94171.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

gives the following expressions for ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} & =-{x}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

By solving the second equation for ${x}_{1}$ and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & ={y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2} \\  & =(-{y}_{2})^{2}+4(-{y}_{2})({y}_{1}+3{y}_{2}) \\  & ={y}_{2}^{2}-4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}-12{y}_{2}^{2} \\  & =-11{y}_{2}^{2}-4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Given that [y1y2]=[31−10][x1x2], express the quadratic form Q(x)=x12+4x1x2 in terms of the components of y.

a
−9y12−4y1y2
b
−12y22−2y1y2
c
−11y22−4y1y2
d
8y22−8y1y2
e
−12y12−4y1y2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that

[y1y2]=[31−10][x1x2]

gives the following expressions for y1 and y2:

y1=3x1+x2y2=−x1

By solving the second equation for x1 and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for x1 and x2:

x1=−y2x2=y1+3y2

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

Q(x)=x12+4x1x2=(−y2)2+4(−y2)(y1+3y2)=y22−4y1y2−12y22=−11y22−4y1y2

q-94184.name: Question 3
q-94184.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $P$ above. Find the matrix of the quadratic form ${x}^{T}\,Ax$ in the basis that consists of the columns of $P.$
q-94184.worked_solution:
Recall that if $x=[{x}_{1},{x}_{2}]^{T}$ is a vector given by its coordinates in the standard basis and $y=[{y}_{1},{y}_{2}]^{T}$ is the same vector but given in the coordinates relative to the basis that consists of the columns of $P,$ then 

$$
x=Py.
$$

As a result, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =(Py)^{T}\,A\,(Py) \\  & =({y}^{T}{P}^{T})\,A\,(Py) \\  & ={y}^{T}({P}^{T}\,AP)\,y,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that the matrix of our form in the new basis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{T}\,AP & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that if $x=[{x}_{1},{x}_{2}]^{T}$ is a vector given by its coordinates in the standard basis and $y=[{y}_{1},{y}_{2}]^{T}$ is the same vector but given in the coordinates relative to the basis that consists of the columns of $P,$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =(Py)^{T}\,A\,(Py) \\  & =({y}^{T}{P}^{T})\,A\,(Py) \\  & ={y}^{T}({P}^{T}\,AP)\,y,\end{aligned}

$$

q-140939.problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-{x}_{2}^{2}$ in terms of the components of $y.$
q-140939.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

gives the following expressions for ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =-2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} & =-{x}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

By solving the second equation for ${x}_{1}$ and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & ={y}_{1}-2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2(-{y}_{2})^{2}+(-{y}_{2})({y}_{1}-2{y}_{2})-({y}_{1}-2{y}_{2})^{2} \\  & =2{y}_{2}^{2}-{y}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}^{2}-{y}_{1}^{2}+4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}-4{y}_{2}^{2} \\  & =-{y}_{1}^{2}+3{y}_{1}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Given that [y1y2]=[−21−10][x1x2], express the quadratic form Q(x)=2x12+x1x2−x22 in terms of the components of y.

a
y12−4y1y2+4y22
b
y12+4y1y2−8y22
c
−y12+3y1y2
d
−y12+3y1y2+8y22
e
y12+5y1y2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that

[y1y2]=[−21−10][x1x2]

gives the following expressions for y1 and y2:

y1=−2x1+x2y2=−x1

By solving the second equation for x1 and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for x1 and x2:

x1=−y2x2=y1−2y2

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

Q(x)=2x12+x1x2−x22=2(−y2)2+(−y2)(y1−2y2)−(y1−2y2)2=2y22−y2y1+2y22−y12+4y1y2−4y22=−y12+3y1y2
